body:
Tested locally (rebased on top of `master` https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/af2c713971499953373380b9ae8673f64423bd59), it works as expected.

Some feedback:

- **Target Coverage** should be hidden when **Preserve Alpha Test Coverage** is unchecked, using a similar approach to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104325 (and modifying `_get_option_visibility()`).
- **Target Coverage** should use a hint range of `0.01` to `0.99`, as values of `0.0` and `1.0` appear to do nothing even when **Preserve Alpha Test Coverage** is checked.

Tested locally, it doesn't seem to work on my end. Enabling the option doesn't seem to have any effect. The material on the left uses a texture without **Preserve Alpha Test**, while the one on the right has it enabled: **Testing project:** [test-alpha-scissor-import.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31189151/test-alpha-scissor-import.zip)

Code looks good to me.

One remaining thing is to recommend the use of this import option in these descriptions:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/bfae01d184c6168b55d48caefa19d5cda6c8ba10/doc/classes/BaseMaterial3D.xml#L587-L589

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/bfae01d184c6168b55d48caefa19d5cda6c8ba10/doc/classes/BaseMaterial3D.xml#L84-L86 with the `alpha_test_threshold` ideally set to match `alpha_scissor_threshold`.
Looks good to me once it is rebased to resolve conflicts
